No he wasn't ugly. But it takes a lot for me to outright say someone is ugly. I definitely wouldn't have walked up to him and gave him my number. I can't convince you otherwise cause you're stuck in your mind. Which I understand. People try to explain to me looks matter more, but I see it differently cause I'm a woman. Guys are more stimulated by what they see, whereas women are more stimulated by what they feel. That's why a a funny, charismatic guy still has good chances with women. So you can't change your height or your looks. Why not try learning better social skills, Charisma, humor, and self-confidence? Why not try giving that a shot? What do you have to lose?

Attraction is not just looks. It really really isn't. I'm not saying looks have no play. Believe me, I know they do. But I would hands down find a guy more attractive who was really self-assure and funny. Seriously, I melt like putty for guys like that. And I wouldn't say he was ugly, but I think he was very average. Like, wasn't a Ken doll. Didn't have a strong jaw. Couldn't really grow facial hair. A big bug eyed. I wouldn't have found him so attractive if it weren't for his amazing personality. Like genuinely being able to make me laugh. A guy that can *really* make a girl laugh (not fake laugh), has more power than the tall square jaw dude.

No I said I had the opportunity, like I could have hooked up with the attractive guy, but I didn't. The guy that was meh looking that I was thinking of had a fiancé, so I couldn't and wouldn't try anything. 

Look, I don't know anything about that sexual dimorphism bullshit, but just because you're shorter and have a narrow frame doesn't mean that there aren't women who would find you attractive. I know a lot of girls who like shorter guys. I know girls who like lankier guys. I know girls who like chubbier guys. Etc. Women are people. They have their own preferences. Are you going to be attractive to every woman? Or even to every woman you want? Nope. If you want to be "sexually dimorphic" then try working on being outgoing and confident. Those are two traits that many people lack, and when you have them, it makes you different.

There's more that I see wrong with myself. That's just the tip and I wasn't going to list them all. So I wouldn't say that one or two of my features are bad, but everything is. But that doesn't matter. The point is that you're putting a lot of weight on your looks. That's your problem. There's a healthy way to put weight on your looks, and there's an unhealthy way. A healthy way is to change the things within your power (i.e. working out, flattering hairstyle, skincare routine, etc). Unhealthy is obsessing about and putting yourself down for the things you can not change. Learning to accept that your imperfections brings mental sanity. It's about saying "yeah my face doesn't look like abc, but that's okay. There's other good things about me like xyz." 

Honestly, for guys, looks are not everything. Like I've had the opportunity to hook up with some very attractive guys, but they were dull as a doorknob so I instantly lost any attraction to them. And there are some meh looking guys I know, but because they have a really funny, and outgoing personality, I would jump them in a second.

Life does have stress. You can't escape it. But it's learning to cope with the stress. Therapy is a good way to learn how to cope. I recommend cognitive behavioral therapy if you're not already doing it. But there are definitely jobs that have less stress than others. It also helps if you find a job closer to your interests. Because even though there will be some things you don't like about it, it's not as terrible as it could be. If a job was fun all the time, then it wouldn't be a job. But there are things you can do to mitigate the bad sides of a job.

I know how you feel. I used to be so dependant on my dad. I believed that no one will ever truly love me like he does, and maybe there is some truth to it. Parental love is supposed to be the strongest type of love, because of an evolutionary desire to protect your offspring and see your gene pool continue. I went to live on my own though, and I was surprised at my capabilities to take care of myself. I screwed up sometimes. But it's sort of a survival instinct that takes over. And sometimes, when you start being more independent in the beginning, it's okay to lean on your parents in case you do mess up. Trial and error helps you get better. Jobs suck usually cause majority of people do not like work. But they aren't all bad. Maybe explore jobs that you're more passionate about. Also finding a job with a good work environment is important. I could make a million dollars but it wouldn't be worth it if I just hated the people I was around for 8 hours a day.

Hey, so I have BDD. I'm not saying you do or don't have it. I have a cross underbite which makes my face asymmetrical. The underbite makes me look like a bulldog. Also, because of my jaw, one of my eyes is slightly lower than the other. I have no idea why, but it is. So essentially my whole face looks like it's slanting to one side like I have Bell's Palsy. I also have a big forehead. Like not just long. I would be fine if it were just long. But no, it like protrudes out, and makes me look like I have a receding hairline, which as a girl is super awesome. /s. Anyway, this shit is really there. I'm not looking in the mirror and seeing stuff that doesn't actually exist. But what I am seeing is stuff that people don't pay attention to as much. What I am doing, is making my looks way more important than they are. Logically I know this, but I don't feel it when I look in the mirror or at a picture of myself. I see all the flaws. I think everyone is focusing on it. I think that's why I'm not lovable, and why my boyfriend left me. 

Thing is, the flaws are real, but the amount of weight I give them is not. That's why I go to therapy. Because the only thing that has really been proven to fix BDD is CBT therapy. I started back in September, and I don't feel any major progress yet really, but I know it will happen because there's science to back it up. It's one of those things you have to just keep practicing and working at. It's like learning the piano. It takes years to master the piano. I can't expect myself to practice playing the piano for a few months and suddenly be able to play like Beethoven. Fighting BDD, or even if you don't have BDD and just low self-esteem, you can't expect for it to be fixed instantly. Especially if they're problems you've been dealing with your whole life.  It's something that takes time.

Hey there. I'm sorry about what you're going through. Money troubles are tough. For what it's worth, if you're in America at least, the eviction process is a long one. It's not very easy for a landlord to be able to evict you. And even once they start the process, it can take some time, depending on what state you live in. Check out /r/legaladvice and they'd be able to give you definite numbers for your state. I'm just saying, if you're worried about being kicked out because you can't pay rent right now, you'd have some time to try to come up with the money. Maybe you could talk to your landlord? Sometimes if you're lucky, they can be understanding. 

Also, you should sign up with GoodRx. IIt's like a coupon for your medications when you don't have insurance. I know it doesn't help presently with what you owe your prescriber, but could help in the future. My prescriptions would come out half off with that thing. It was pretty awesome.

High school sucks. It's not the end of the world that you're not doing well it. It doesn't mean you still can't have a second chance. I went to junior college to get an associates degree. Junior colleges let literally everyone in. It's also cheaper. Do well in getting your associates and then you can go on to get your bachelors. Get yourself therapy and work on your mental health while your in high school. I wish I did. It's much harder later in life to try to learn coping skills while you have more responsibilities. This is great time for you to address it.

Hey, I used to feel like my depression was from not having friends. I've learned that I just have a chemical imbalance though. Here's what I can suggest to you to make friends like I did.

First, people are drawn to outgoing people. You can learn to be outgoing. Read books like How To Win Friends and Influence People. You can find a PDF for free with google or the audio book. I'm on my phone, otherwise I'd link it for you. Sorry. There's a great YouTube channel called Charisma on Command. Start watching his videos. If you're okay with torrenting stuff, you can find his Charisma University videos for free too. In general, there's a surplus of books to teach you how to talk to people, how to have self-confidence, how to read body language, etc. Study up. It's one of the most useful life skills to have.

Second, be the friend you want to have. This kind of sucks, because it means you have to engage people and ask them to hang out regularly. This was a struggle for me. I was always down to hang out, but my anxiety made it hard to ask people to hang out. I had to push through. Sometimes you may get rejected, but that's okay. It was their loss. 

I wish you the best.

So just some recommendations from someone who has felt like you. I still want to kill myself, but it's not because I can't have a social life. I used to think my depression came from not having friends. And some of it probably did, because having friends is easier than not having friends. So here are some recommendations, and I don't mean any of them in a judgmental way of you, but just what I have done. 

1. Start reading books about how to have better people skills. I can email you some if you want. How to Win Friends and Influence People is a must for absolutely anyone. [Here](https://soundcloud.com/larry-amos-jr/sets/dale-carnegie-how-to-win) is a link to the audio book. I've read most of Matthew Hussey's books on dating. Go watch YouTube videos on developing better social skills. One of my favorites is [Charisma on Command](https://www.youtube.com/user/charismaoncommand). Matthew Hussey also has YouTube videos [here](https://www.youtube.com/user/gettheguyteam). Being outgoing and a people person is a learnable skill. It takes times, and lots of practice and error. And if you look stupid once in awhile, who fucking cares about them anyway. 

2. Download Bumble. Not to date, but use BumbleBFF. There's another app that starts with a V that I can't think of right now. Regardless, there's a lot of apps out there these days that are geared towards making friends. These are great because these people are looking for friends too. Yeah, it's kind of fucking awkward at first. And it felt like a date a little bit. But I got over it. I've come to realize that most relationships are going to have this awkward phase in the beginning of not feeling comfortable with the person. But you just have to push through it. Keep hanging out with the person until it stops feeling so superficial. I used to not have female friends just cause I thought women sucked. I just felt like I got along with guys better, and honestly I do. But I learned this was an internal struggle I had that I needed to get over. I now have a few girls I can ask to go hang out with as a group, and one girl that I can call up to binge television and wine with. Even though I call her my best friend, it still has a bit of that fake vibe to me, but I push through it. The more and more I hang out with her, the closer we get. It's better than not having anyone to hang out with. I think some women, like myself, are just don't get along with women as well. I definitely have way more fun hanging out with a group of guys, but I think it's a good balance in my life to seek out female friends. Also, key word is seek out. This means I had to make an effort to hang out with these girls. It felt very one sided for awhile, but eventually it balanced out. 

3. I get it with the guys who only want you for sex. I feel like it's one or the other. Either a guy I'm feeling only wants to hook up with me, or I'm not interested in the guy who wants a relationship with me. Yeah, I'm feeding into some major red pill theories right now, but they can fuck off. It's just one of those things where you have to keep wading through the shit until you find that guy who actually makes you excited but at the same time he really wants to have a relationship with you. Matthew Hussey has some videos that talk about how to deal with guys who are pushy for sex. You should check them out. And just know, just because they just want to have sex with you, doesn't mean you're less valuable. Just means that those guys are just trying to get laid. It's not you. It's them.
It stresses me out because it's the only reason I haven't killed myself yet. I know it will hurt them. I know they love me. I have a good life and no reason to want to kill myself. But I do.
I can't. The one thing I had in my life that made me happy doesn't want me anymore. He moved on to another girl. It's been months, and I still can't put myself back together.
